title: Console backlog: Hopscotch prioritization & cutlist (Jun 2026)
content:
Purpose:
- Create a minimal, actionable cutlist from the Console backlog for next 3 sprints (hopscotch cadence). This doc captures triage rationale, tradeoffs, wireframe writeups for the highest-value items, estimates, and owners.

Context:
- Q2 product goal: reduce token-debug time-to-resolution for customers by improving per-route observability and rollout UX.
- We have ~48 console tickets flagged for UX/ops polish; this doc picks a pragmatic path to ship high-impact items while deferring or cutting lower ROI work.
- Hopscotch approach: alternate between small UX polish sprints and one deeper infrastructure/ops sprint so we keep visible velocity and also unblock Dedicated/Private customers.

Meeting notes (brainstorm + triage, 2026-06-10):
- Present: Aisha (PM), Marco (Design), Sofia (ENG lead), Liam (SRE), Devon (Solutions).
- Outcome: Prioritize observability route improvements + rollout confidence features; cut or defer multi-tenant large rework and low-usage admin features.

Triage matrix (informal):
- Criteria: customer impact, engineering effort, cross-team dependency, risk to SLAs, time-to-value.
- Scoring: H/M/L per criterion -> quick product score and final priority. (used to pick top 10).

Top prioritized items (cutlist):
1) Route diagnostics: token-level timeline view (PROD-2378) — HIGH
   - Why: Frequently requested by customer support for reproducing latency/cost anomalies.
   - Proposed scope (cutlist): implement read-only timeline with token timestamps, model variant, and route config at top-level. NO edit-in-place, NO playback.
   - Wireframe: single-pane timeline, left column request metadata, center scrollable token timeline with hover tooltips (token, latency, batching ID), right column quick-links to logs and trace ID.
   - Acceptance criteria: support for last 30 days, filter by route, model, and user token. 95th percentile load test verified for list of 50 concurrent viewers.
   - Estimate: 8 story points (M). Owner: Sofia.

2) Canary rollout checklist + health overlay (UX-942) — HIGH
   - Why: Reduces risk of bad deploys; used during Dedicated rollouts.
   - Cutlist: surface a checklist of pre-checks + live health strip (error rate, latency, token-rate) and a single-click rollback. Defer: multi-arm A/B analytics.
   - Wireframe notes: small floating panel in rollout modal showing 3 green/red indicators; click expands to timeline.
   - Acceptance: canary creation shows checklist, health overlay updates at 10s cadence, rollback executes policy in <= 60s.
   - Estimate: 5 story points (S). Owner: Devon.

3) Per-route cost breakdown (agg) — MEDIUM
   - Why: Product teams ask for clearer token/unit cost per route to track spend.
   - Cutlist: aggregated cost last-7d, suggested optimizations (batching suggestions link to Optimize). Defer: per-prompt-level drilldown.
   - Acceptance: CSV export + chart; baseline cost calc and suggested optimization flag.
   - Estimate: 5-8 SP. Owner: Aisha.

4) Quick-search for routes + fuzzy match (internal UX ticket) — MEDIUM
   - Why: Console navigation is slow for customers with 100+ routes.
   - Cutlist: implement fuzzy search and keyboard shortcut. Defer: persistent pinned lists.
   - Estimate: 3 SP. Owner: Marco.

5) Alerts authoring UX cleanup (small) — MEDIUM
   - Why: Alerts get misconfigured; small UX fixes will reduce noisiness.
   - Cutlist: merge threshold fields, inline validation, add example presets.
   - Estimate: 2 SP. Owner: Marco.

Deferred / cut items (explicitly deprioritized):
- Full per-token playback with audio/video simulation (high eng cost) — cut to backlog.
- Multi-tenant admin RBAC overhaul (huge infra dependency) — defer to Q4.
- Rewriting rollout analytics pipeline for fine-grained A/B (defer).

Wireframe writeups (concise):
- Token timeline (PROD-2378) visual spec:
  - Top bar: route selector, date range, model variant toggles.
  - Left meta column: request ID, user, API key, client version, route config snapshot.
  - Timeline canvas: horizontally scrollable, each bubble = token emission; color = token type (user/assistant/system); size = latency; hover card = {token, ts, latency, batch id, kv-cache-hit}.
  - Right tools column: links: open trace, open logs, open evals, download request payload.
  - Mobile behavior: timeline collapses to dense list; allow filter only.

- Canary checklist overlay (UX-942) visual spec:
  - Button in rollout modal: "Checklist & health" -> panel with 3 states (Ready, Attention, Blocked).
  - Health strip: small stacked bars showing p95 latency, error %, and token QPS.
  - Rollback CTA: red secondary button with confirmation modal.

Acceptance criteria style (used across cutlist):
- Clear owner and no more than 3 acceptance tests per item.
- Performance guardrails included for observability features.
- No experimental feature flags unless necessary.

Estimates and sprint mapping (hopscotch plan):
- Sprint A (2026-06-22 -> 2026-07-05): token timeline MVP (start backend + UI), quick-search, alerts cleanup.
  - Goals: ship read-only timeline stub + search + alerts small UX.
  - Capacity assumption: 2 FE, 2 BE, 1 SRE half-time.
- Sprint B (2026-07-06 -> 2026-07-19): canary checklist + per-route cost agg + polish timeline.
  - Goals: rollout checklist shipped to canary users; cost view basic chart.
- Sprint C (2026-07-20 -> 2026-08-02): buffer / infra sprint for telemetry, perf tuning, and any hotfixes.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: timeline data volume will expose performance issues in Trace store.
  - Mitigation: limit initial date range to 30 days + sample 1/10 for heatmap; SRE to run perf tests before rollout.
- Risk: adding one-click rollback could be dangerous for Dedicated customers with custom policies.
  - Mitigation: require policy confirmation and restrict rollback to users with deploy permissions.

Open questions (action owners):
- Q1: Should token timeline pull from the same trace store or a denormalized view? -> Action: Sofia to prototype both (due 2026-06-18).
- Q2: Analytics needs for canary: do we need raw event export day-0? -> Action: Devon to confirm with Solutions (due 2026-06-15).
- Q3: Does cost agg use per-token pricing or custom contract tiers? -> Action: Aisha to stash pricing mapping (due 2026-06-16).

Next steps (immediate):
- Create sprint tickets using the cutlist and attach wireframe snippets (Aisha) by 2026-06-13.
- Design to produce final mocks for token timeline + canary overlay (Marco) by 2026-06-16.
- Engineering spike: data model for token timeline (Sofia) 2d spike.
- SRE to schedule perf test window (Liam) before first canary rollout.

Notes to self (PM rough):
- Keep scope small: user value from read-only timeline + quick rollback > fancy playback.
- Track customer asks: attach recent support threads to PROD-2378 for prioritization context.
- Use Hopscotch label in PRs so we can search shipped features for release notes.

Relevant links/refs: PROD-2378 (ticket), UX-942 (canary checklist), PR #412 (ui scaffold), confluence rollout page.

Revision history:
- 2026-06-08 created initial hopscotch idea and seed list.
- 2026-06-10 triage call, updated priorities.
- 2026-06-12 added estimates and mapping to sprints.
